questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring new ways of learning and other opportunities within my field, creating new connections and experience living in another country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, mostly. Some if it was confusing, especially due to the sheer amount of information you have to deal with. Some of the deadlines were communicated in a confusing manner.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help from my tenant union; how to settle in at my new place and so on. I also received some help from my receiving university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, as the university had a lot of housing options available to exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In this case, it was not difficult, as there was a direct tram to the university campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was not too complicated. I had to sign up for courses that were pre-approved, and upon arrival, get a student card.

Only difficulties were with selecting courses, as it was difficult to find out which were available to exchange students and which were not - this was not communicated so clearly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were help available through normal student advisory services.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were confusing elements, such as some courses at first seemingly being available to exchange students, and then later it turns out they were not. This led to me accidentally signing up for a master course that was not available to me, and I lose out on choosing a course I was really interested in as a result.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be careful about your choices during the pre-approval, as it it's difficult to get access to courses later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took bachelor courses, but one of my courses were unofficially a master course I think - or a mix, since mostly master students took this course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar, but more "flipped classroom" style teaching than I'm used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: GEOV210 Plate Tectonics, GEOV217 Geohazards and GEOV251 Advanced Structural Geology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend especially the geohazard and structural geology course; it's a great opportunity to learn about the local geology and circumstances that are not thought as much at least in my own university. Even the plate tectonics course taught a lot about the local geological development.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was expensive to buy food, and I had to buy local phone plan as halfway through my own phone company cancelled my plan due to higher usage outside of my home country. There were expenses to student trips and student clubs as well..

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food more expensive. Books were not more expensive than in my own country.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of student clubs, which was nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of activities available to students, including at the student housing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some of the student clubs, especially the sports clubs. Also join the Sammen gym. The university hiking club is a bit pretentious, and not recommended to people who aren't into extreme sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The nature and mountains surrounding Bergen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy, as it's similar to my own.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and activities, it can be hard to make friends without doing something together, as people aren't very outgoing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that people are more reserved.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were kind, helpful and easy to be around.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Consider your pre-approval courses as your final choices, explore the nature around the city and join some of the university activities to make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy the monthly plan for the bybane transport.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature and the teaching at university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Breaking through and making friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
